result.nttCn: 2009년부터 실시한 태안 마도해역의 탐사조사 보고서입니다. 마도해역 탐사는 2009년부터 난행량을 비롯한 마도 해역을 중심으로 꾸준히 진행해 왔으며, 그 결과를 바탕으로 2009년 마도1호선, 2010년 마도2호선에 이어 2011년 마도3호선까지 발굴하는 커다란 성과를 거두었습니다. 보고서는 I. 머리말 / II. 조사방법 및 내용 / III. 탐사인양유물 / IV. 맺음말 등으로 구성하였습니다. *담당부서 : 수중발굴과
result.nttCnEn: National Research Institute of Maritime Cultural Heritage has been conducting exploration projects in the waters of Mado, including nanhaengnyang, since 2009, when local fishermen reported the discovery of cultural assets. These exploration projects led to great achievements - the excavation of Mado Shipwerck No.1 in 2009, Mado Shipwerck No.2 in 2010, and Mado Shipwerck No. 3 in 2011. Conducting exploration projects together with underwater excavations in the waters of Mado resulted in the excavation of many relics. Leading relics that were discovered as a result of the exploration projects are stone anchors and pottery wares. Stone anchors have been excavated since 2009. To date, a total 68 stone anchors have been excavated. stone anchors were an essential tool of vessels. The other leading relicis pottery. Various pottery wares were discovered, many of them from dierent eras and areas. Some are from Korea, while others are from China. They were made in dierent eras as proven by the discovery of initial celadon wares and modern ceramic wares. What we should take special note of is the excavation of Chinese ceramic wares with a Chinese character inscription in the bottom, made using black ink. What was inscribed was the family names and written seals of merchants who conducted international maritime trade during the Song and Yuan Dynasties of China. The Goryeo Dynasty actively engaged in maritime trade with China. The excavated pottery wares are proof.
